facts.text: Petworth takes its name from the 205‑acre estate of John Tayloe III, likely inspired by the English town of Petworth in West Sussex.
The neighborhood masterfully blends historic rowhouses with a modern, vibrant arts scene, making it feel both timeless and contemporary.
Sherman Circle, the heart of Petworth, serves as a community gathering spot that reflects the area’s inclusive spirit.
Petworth’s historic rowhouses line tree‑lined streets, each building showcasing unique craftsmanship that tells the story of the neighborhood’s past.
Room 808, a minority‑owned comedy club on Upshur Street, has earned recognition from The Washington Post as one of D.C.’s best comedy venues.
In the early 19th century, John Tayloe III kept horses for races at the Washington Jockey Club, a club he founded with Charles Carnan Ridgely.
